Here you go. The graph is a bit outdated. We've now reached 400ppm of CO2 and continue to constantly break record global temperatures. You really need to go far far back when the composition of the Earth was radically different to get rid of the link between CO2 and temperature since other factors were able to overwhelm it in a world that resembled very little the one we live in today.

There's actually a specific reason for this as well too. Most don't know but the link between CO2 and temperature isn't just a correlation. CO2 has a unique characteristic. It is nonreactive to shortwave radiation, but absorbs and reemits (or in other words blocks) longwave radiation. The reason this is relevant is because energy from the sun hits our planet in the form of shortwave radiation. But when it's reemitted back off the Earth it comes off in infrared or longwave radiation. CO2 lets the heat in, but then stops it from leaving.

I didn't really have a major opinion on this topic one way or another for some time, but the physical explanation for the functioning of the greenhouse gases in relation to forms of radiation is what really was an eye opener for me. There's no hand waving or modeling involved. You pump CO2 into an atmosphere you're going to heat things up. This is for instance where the insane sounding idea from Elon Musk of terraforming Mars by dropping nukes on its ice caps came from. The Martian ice caps are heavily composed of dry ice, which is frozen CO2. Melt the ice caps and you convert the CO2 into gas which not only thickens the atmosphere but begins to heat up the planet.
